title: Filter using a condition
summary: filter keeps rows for which a function returns True. The function receives a row and checks the condition you chose.
introduction: filter keeps rows for which a function returns True. The function receives a row and checks the condition you chose. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: filter keeps rows for which a function returns True. The function receives a row and checks the condition you chose.

blocks.code:
from datasets import Dataset
data = Dataset.from_dict({"text": ["moon", "sun", "stars"]})
long_words = data.filter(lambda row: len(row["text"]) > 3)
print(list(long_words["text"]))
blocks.title: Filter using a condition

blocks.text: The output is ['moon', 'stars']. Their lengths are 4 and 5, both greater than 3. sun has length 3 and is removed from this result.
